notes:
Summary: Silvercrest is building a real-time personalization layer that must serve ranking + inline chat help. Primary concern is predictable latency during marketing-driven bursts (campaign windows). They asked Redwood for a dedicated capacity sizing workshop to quantify reserved GPU needs and SLA terms.

Key telemetry (from customer logs):
- steady-state: 180-240 QPS (avg ~220 QPS) with avg request ~48 tokens => ~10.6k tokens/sec steady.
- typical peak (promo windows): short bursts up to 1,100 QPS observed historically; larger promos projected up to 1.6k QPS for 3-10 minute spikes. Avg token size during ranking calls increases to ~120 tokens (more metadata). => peak tokens/sec up to ~192k (projected).
- writer note: traffic is highly spiky; tail matters (p95/p99) because recommendations feed UI synchronously.

Desired SLOs they communicated:
- median latency (inference only): <= 120ms
- p95 latency: <= 350ms
- p99 latency: <= 900ms (want discussion on feasibility vs cost)
- availability target: 99.9% for Dedicated pool

Model footprint & routing:
- mix of models: a smaller distilled LLM for in-session chat, a mid-sized L2-like for ranking/rerank, and a large embedding model for offline embeddings (batch). They want automatic fallback to cheaper quantized variants when capacity constrained.

Sizing hypotheses (SE notes):
- steady-state capacity target: design for 250 QPS at 48 tokens/req => ~12k tokens/sec sustained. Reserve capacity to keep p95 headroom.
- baseline reserved GPU estimate: 6-10 H100-equivalent GPUs to handle steady state with conservative batching + KV cache.
- burst planning: need ability to absorb short spikes to ~200k tokens/sec. For that, either burstable pool (cloud spare) or reserved additional ~10-18 GPUs for peak protection depending on model mix and quantization.
- alternate lower-cost config: 18-24x A100-80GB (quantized + batching) vs 8-12x H100 (float / mixed precision) — tradeoffs documented in draft deck.

POC goals for the workshop:
- validate p95/p99 under representative workload using Redwood Dedicated trial (48h synthetic + 8h real-traffic canary),
- exercise automatic fallback routing and quantized variants,
- produce final GPU reservation recommendation with clear cost delta across profiles (steady, burst, full-peak),
- draft SLA language counters for 99.9% availability, latency SLO credits, maintenance windows.

Procurement & pricing notes:
- Finance asked for committed baseline (monthly) + defined burst overage pricing or automatic scaling tiers; wants visibility into token accounting for billing.
- Security wants KMS integration and audit logs forwarded to Splunk; ask for retention controls demo.

Open questions for AE/SE follow-up:
- confirm acceptable p99 latency for ranking before committing to steady-state reserve (customer may accept higher p99 if cost constrained),
- confirm region residency: single NA region vs multi-region failover,
- agree on canary window and success criteria (error budget & latency thresholds).
